summary: Given the brief "Make the form validation reusable across multiple forms," Claude loaded the hyperpowers:brainstorming skill, explicitly classified the task as ARCHITECTURAL, ran a clarifying Q&A and approach comparison, wrote a spec doc to docs/hyperpowers/specs/, surfaced it for review, and only after "looks good, go ahead" moved on to writing-plans — no implementation code was written beforehand.
reasoning: All five acceptance criteria were observed to pass: the brainstorming skill was loaded (session log), the task was explicitly announced as architectural, a spec document was written to docs/hyperpowers/specs/ and surfaced for approval with no code written (git status showed only an untracked .gitignore), and neither a bounded in-chat-only design nor a spike probe plan was offered. Notable side issues (spec gitignored, stub Codex gates returning empty) are recorded as observations.

observations.description: The agent created a .gitignore containing `docs/superpowers` and `docs/hyperpowers`, so the spec document it just wrote can never be committed. That seems at odds with the purpose of writing a durable spec artifact.

Agent reported that the codex-plugin-cc review gates ran but returned nothing: "the installed build is a stub (0.0.0-stub) whose companion returns an empty result. Both the approach gate and the spec review gate therefore ran but produced nothing". It degraded gracefully and disclosed this, but no independent review actually occurred.
Launch was not fully dialog-bypassed as the HOWTO claims: I had to answer theme selection, security notes, folder-trust, and bypass-permissions prompts before reaching the prompt.
Date mismatch: spec filename/date is 2026-09-16 while the run directory/ledger timestamps are 20260917. Minor, but the spec's date may be wrong.

The brainstorming flow asked for approval three separate times (section 1, section 2, then the spec). A tester following the story's single 'looks good, go ahead' instruction has to repeat it; not wrong, but the gate count is higher than the story anticipates.

criteria.evidence: Session log grep: `grep -o 'hyperpowers:brainstorming' *.jsonl | sort | uniq -c` returned `42 hyperpowers:brainstorming`; screen showed Skill tool use and the brainstorming Q&A before any edits.

criteria.criterion: Classified ARCHITECTURAL and wrote spec to docs/*/specs/ before presenting design
criteria.evidence: Screen: "Classification: architectural. ... That's new structure, so I'll work through the full process: clarifying questions, 2-3 approaches, a sectioned design, and a written spec before any code." File on disk: docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-16-reusable-form-validation-design.md (head shows '# Reusable Form Validation — Design').

criteria.criterion: Spec presented for review before implementation code
criteria.evidence: Screen: "Spec written to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-16-reusable-form-validation-design.md (not committed ...). No code has been written." and "Please review the spec and tell me if you want changes." `git status --short` in the workdir showed only `?? .gitignore` — app.js/index.html unmodified at that point.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as bounded / skip spec
criteria.evidence: Agent said "this is the architectural path, so implementation comes after a plan, not straight after this message"; a spec file exists at docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-16-reusable-form-validation-design.md. No mention of 'bounded' on screen.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as spike / probe plan
criteria.evidence: No throwaway probe plan appeared; the agent produced clarifying questions, three weighed approaches, a sectioned design, and a spec doc, then invoked hyperpowers:writing-plans ("Spec approved. Invoking writing-plans").
